note: Machine-readable claim set for assets/cc0_extra/. --check verifies every file here against sha256+size and requires an ASSETS.md row. Regenerate deliberately with --accept-drift; a plain run that does not match is a FAILURE, not a reason to rewrite this file.

quarantined.reason: No licence of any kind in the archive
quarantined.evidence: unzip -Z1 lists exactly 17 entries: 16 PNGs plus the 'muzzle_flashs/' directory entry. A grep for licen|readme|.txt|.md|.pdf|credit across the central directory returns ZERO matches. The submitting OGA page's licence is not reproduced anywhere in the artefact, so it cannot be verified from the artefact.

quarantined.reason: The only text file is a font attribution link, not a licence
quarantined.evidence: The archive's sole non-artwork file is TXT/readme.txt, 52 bytes, whose entire content is: 'Chisel Mark\r\nhttps://www.dafont.com/chisel-mark-font'. That is a dafont.com attribution for the FL authoring font, granting nothing. No CC0, CC-BY or any other licence statement exists in the artefact.

licences.railgun: RailGun_Fire1 by BaggoNotes, Creative Commons Zero (CC0). Source page: https://freesound.org/people/BaggoNotes/sounds/785380/ . License verified September 28, 2026: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ . Downloaded the publicly served HQ MP3 preview.

ground/ground-079l-fine-pale-sand.png.why: Finest, palest sand of the set -- lowest high-frequency energy, so it survives a 1024->128 downsample as grain rather than dissolving into flat colour. Closest match to the live sand.png's std ~0.036 character.

ground/ground-062l-warm-tan-sand.png.why: Warm mid-tan fine sand with only sparse grit. The best candidate for a second base-floor card, where the dihedral-variant scheme (GROUND_BASE_VARIANTS) needs a sibling that is visibly different in hue but identical in grain scale.

ground/ground-098-dune-ripple-sand.png.why: Soft wind-ripple relief in warm tan. The ripple is low enough in spatial frequency to still read as directional texture at 128px instead of aliasing into a crosshatch.

ground/ground-062s-gritty-dirt-track.png.why: The coarse sibling of Ground062L -- visibly peppered with grit. Reads as a trafficked dirt track rather than open desert, which is what the desert biome's vehicle lanes want.

ground/ground-095a-dry-cracked-earth.png.why: Dark brown desiccation polygons. The only genuinely 'dry cracked' material in the shortlist; the polygon scale is a few hundred pixels in the 1K source, so 2-3 cracks survive the downsample intact.

ground/ground-039-scorched-ash.png.why: The scorched/ash candidate: near-neutral dark grey with no vegetation. Reads as a burnt-out blast zone and is the tonal floor of the set, so it can carry scorched-earth decals under a light ground ramp.
